d.d: To persuade someone to do something which they are reluctant to do, especially by flattery or promises; to coax.
simple past and past participle of cajole
present participle and gerund of cajole
d.x: The zookeeper was cajoling the lion back into its cage.

d.d: The act of one who cajoles.
d.x: Threats and cajolings failed to convince her.

d.d: A large valley surrounded by mountains of considerable height (especially in Latin America), through which a river runs.
A member of the ethnic group descending from Acadia, primarily French-speaking Catholic and living in Southern Louisiana and Maine.
Relating to the Cajun people or their culture.
Of spicy food prepared in the style of the Cajun cuisine.
